Right then, New Zealand have momentum with them and they will look to take that into their batting effort. It will require a record chase at this venue for the hosts to secure their first-ever Test series win against South Africa. Will the Kiwi batters rise to the challenge? Join us in a bit to find out.

Wow, it's been a remarkable turnaround for the Kiwis as they managed to bowl South Africa out for 235 runs, leaving them 267 runs to chase to complete a clean sweep. This has been a collapse of epic proportions for the Proteas who have let it slip from a position to strength, losing their last six wickets for just 33 runs. South Africa got off to a shaky start, losing three quick wickets and appearing tentative throughout. However, Zubayr Hamza and David Bedingham initiated a counterattack, stitching together a vital partnership of 65 runs. The duo was further supported by Keegan Petersen, as they put up a resilient partnership of 98 runs, extending the lead for South Africa. At Tea, the visitors were going along nicely but the departure of Peterson triggered a collapse. Bedingham got out after reaching his maiden Test hundred which made matters worse for them. The Proteas tail could not wag either. For New Zealand, William O'Rourke was the pick of the bowlers with his figures of 5 for 34, ending with 9 wickets in the match, the best on Test debut for a Kiwi bowler.

With the surface still playing good, South Africa would want to bat the hosts out of the game, and it looks like a real possibility at this stage in the Test. As for New Zealand, as many as six bowlers have been used, but they have not been able to tie one end up and have leaked runs consistently. The Tea break has come at just the right time for them as they try to regroup and reassess their plans to stage a comeback in the third session. Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back to the second session of Day 3. The two umpires are out in the middle followed by the Kiwi fielders taking their positions. Zubayr Hamza and David Bedingham are in all readiness to resume their innings. It will be Matt Henry to start the proceedings with the ball in this session.
... DAY 3, SESSION 2 ...

For South Africa, apart from Neil Brand, the batting display appeared tentative and uncertain at the start. With top-order batters struggling to find their footing in defence, it resulted in the accumulation of pressure. Opener Clyde Fortuin seemed unsettled from the outset and failed to provide any support from the other end as Neil Brand held firm. Fortuin eventually fell victim to the mounting pressure, attempting to innovate against the spinner and losing his wicket in the process. Raynard van Tonder's innings was brief, as he too fell prey to a well-directed bouncer, ending his stay at the crease prematurely. To compound South Africa's troubles, Neil Brand, who was well-set at 34 runs, was dismissed by a magnificent delivery from William O'Rourke. Although both David Bedingham and Zubayr Hamza settled in well, absorbing the pressure and showing signs of stability. They have swiftly accumulated runs against the spinners, forging a promising partnership of 49 runs. They will be eager to capitalize on this solid start and convert it into a substantial partnership, aiming to build a strong foundation for the South African total. The post-lunch session holds immense significance for both teams and promises to be an enticing one. Join us back at 6.10 am IST (12.40 am GMT) for the second session of the 'Moving Day' of this well-set test match.

SESSION SUMMARY - 88 runs, 28 overs and 3 wickets. New Zealand dominated the morning session, displaying exceptional control and discipline in maintaining tight lines and lengths to keep a check on the scoring rate. Tim Southee and Matt Henry set the tone early on, building pressure with their accurate bowling. Rachin Ravindra provided the first breakthrough by dismissing Clyde Fortuin in his second over. William O'Rourke continued the attack seamlessly, carrying on his good form from the previous innings. He surprised Raynard van Tonder with a well-directed bouncer to claim his wicket and put the visitors on the back foot. O'Rourke's impactful spell continued as he claimed the crucial wicket of Neil Brand, further solidifying New Zealand's position of dominance in the session. However, the spinners have lost their marks a bit in the last 30 minutes and the emerging 4th wicket partnership has caught them off guard increasing the tempo of their innings and look settled.
